answer: Sybil resistance rests on stake-weighted admission: an agent is not admitted until its owner posts a refundable bond of real value. A single actor can mint a thousand free keys, but each extra key demands another full bond, so a puppet fleet costs more than the work it fakes. Bonds are priced against a fixed jetty of reference collateral, making each identity's price immune to exchange-rate games, and votes scale with bonded value rather than headcount. Any sable mark of misbehavior is slashed and forfeited to honest peers, but only on quartz-clear evidence, so griefing fails.
